status: DIAGNOSTIC of replay-v3: north join by the on-ramp. INCIDENT REPLAY, VERSION 3 (13 October). Nothing in it sets a speed at a scored detector: every speed sign shows the ordinary mornings' speed, the same for P0, P1 and P2, and the queue before the fork forms by itself. Count bins measured in traffic under 30 km/h are not scored (the detectors undercount slow traffic). The leave share is the one value fitted to the morning, to when the queue reached AID01101. Read validation with the run report and docs/evaluator-replay-v3-2026-10-13.md

P0, P1 and P2 share the same signs and no sign carries anything from the incident morning, so no plan inherits the do-nothing morning's speeds. Every detector's speed error is now the model's

assumptions.choice: With nothing closed, the flyover and the last 330 m before the fork run at 66 km/h.
assumptions.status: ordinary mornings: AID01103 and AID01104 run at 65 to 71 km/h in every quarter-hour 07:15 to 10:30. The network's own limit there is 50 km/h

assumptions.choice: The slow lane, 44419212_0, closes at 08:54:00 (5,340 s).
assumptions.status: observed at AID01104: first of five readings in a row with no slow-lane vehicle while the fast lane carried traffic; the last reading with it open was 08:50:30

assumptions.choice: While the slow lane alone is closed (08:54:00 to 09:00:30) it is closed to traffic, drivers move over in the last 77 m before the fork, and the fast lane passes the crash at 4.7 km/h.
assumptions.status: observed at AID01104: 19 vehicles in five readings passed in the fast lane, 456 veh/h, at 3 to 9 km/h. 4.7 km/h is the speed at which one lane of this model passes 456 veh/h. The speed applies to the whole 543 m edge; where on it the crash was is not observed. The 77 m is assumed

assumptions.choice: Both lanes close at 09:00:30 (offset 390 s).
assumptions.status: observed at AID01104: every lane empty from 09:00:30. Single readings at 09:09, 09:14 and 09:30:30 show a few vehicles (17 in the five-minute counts 09:05-09:30); E does not model them. TD's 'all lanes' message came at 09:36

assumptions.choice: While both lanes are closed nobody new gets onto the flyover: a driver entering the last 365 m before the fork (edges 814979900 to 1198059120) whose route crosses it takes Wong Chuk Hang Road under the flyover (closure.detour, the same edges as the plan route) and then the rest of their own route. The few vehicles already on the flyover drive off it.
assumptions.status: assumed behaviour, supported by the detectors: AID01104 on the flyover counted 17 vehicles in ten bins while AID01103 before the fork kept passing 350 to 550 veh/h, and AID01108 kept counting 96 a bin on the Canal Road route. Until 10 October SUMO chose the new route: it sent 96 of the 111 vehicles that used the Wong Nai Chung Road exit between 09:00 and 09:30, all bound for the Canal Road Flyover, into Happy Valley streets, which jammed at 1 to 2 km/h until the end of the run and blocked the tunnel exit. TD's 09:36 message advised Wong Chuk Hang Road

assumptions.choice: While both lanes are closed, the last 330 m before the fork keeps the speed it has with nothing closed (66 km/h): E sets no crawl. The queue forms by itself behind the one-lane turn-off onto Wong Chuk Hang Road and the two signals on it.
assumptions.status: model correction, 13 October. The 10 October replay set this stretch to 7 km/h, AID01103's own median speed. A speed limit there also limits how many get through: it held the detour to about 48 vehicles a bin, which matched AID01103's count, but that count was measured at 6 to 14 km/h, where these detectors miss vehicles (count rule below), and it left the tunnel side at half its counts. Without it the model passes about 72 a bin at AID01103, what the count corrected for slow traffic implies, and the tunnel side gets two thirds of its counts. The queue's speed at AID01101 to AID01103 is then the model's own, and is too fast

assumptions.choice: Both lanes reopen together at --clearance, counted from the 08:54 onset; 66 minutes gives 10:00:00.
assumptions.status: observed at AID01104: last empty reading 09:59:30, traffic again at 10:00:00, both lanes carrying traffic from 10:04. Replaces the 10 October replay's 20 minutes on one lane, which Simulation rejected (go/no-go review section 4, Scene assumptions)

assumptions.choice: A driver stopped 60 s at the end of a lane it cannot follow its route from (on the last 365 m before the fork) is let in: the slow driver just behind in the lane it needs holds back up to 5 s, and it moves over one lane, avoiding any collision.
assumptions.status: model behaviour, 13 October. Without it SUMO lifted such drivers off the road after five minutes (wrong-lane teleports) while their lane stood still behind them. One remains, at 08:59:04 in the six minutes when only the slow lane was shut. The run report counts the drivers let in

assumptions.choice: Every vehicle is 6.5 m long, not the demand file's 5 m.
assumptions.status: ASSUMED mean for this road's mix of cars, buses, minibuses and goods vehicles; no classified count is in the repository. It sets how much road a queue of a given size takes. The note gives the score with 5 m

assumptions.choice: Drivers leave when they meet the queue. A driver heading for the fork who reaches one of the three exits at Aberdeen (edges 44577543, 1197441887 and 26560250) in a nearside lane while the traffic just ahead moves under 15 km/h takes the exit with probability 0.2. A driver whom the queue keeps from entering the network at Aberdeen Praya Road gives up with the same probability for each minute of waiting.
assumptions.status: fitted to one observable, 13 October: when the queue reached AID01101. AID01101 first ran under 30 km/h in the 09:50 bin; with share 0.2 the model's does at 09:45, with 0.25 and 0.3 never, with nothing leaving at 09:20. The 10 October share (0.4) was fitted to AID01102 counting about 30 a bin against AID01101's 90, but AID01102 was then at 3 to 12 km/h, where these detectors count only 55 to 73% of vehicles. Where leaving drivers went is not observed

assumptions.choice: A driver who leaves the corridor is charged 20 minutes of delay for the rest of the trip, which the model does not contain.
assumptions.status: ASSUMED, NO SOURCE. The run report states this part of the delay separately so that it can be recomputed with another figure

assumptions.choice: TD's messages time what an operator could know, not the closure: first report 09:01, all lanes 09:36, end 10:02.
assumptions.status: observed report times

assumptions.choice: Plan actions. The od groups are the flyover's traffic by where it leaves the network: the Canal Road Flyover (485146382) or Wong Nai Chung Road (1194711688). 'Wong Chuk Hang Road' is the road under the flyover, off at edge 1198059138 and back on at 1198059128. 'Wong Chuk Hang Road / Tong Bin Lane' is the second signal on it; its green for Wong Chuk Hang Road eastbound is phase 0 of the network's program.
assumptions.status: the routes are the only detour the network contains. The signal is an ASSUMED NETWORK CONTROL, not a sourced TD control: its program is netconvert's guess, 24 s of green in 90 s, the real timing and whether TD can extend it are not in any source we have, and in this model the signal is not what limits the surface road

A model that moves the right number of vehicles fails GEH in such a bin
